correctness.rationale: Exact derivatives prove a unique global depth minimizer for every positive attenuation and the boundary 1/21. The increasing bijective scaled coordinate reduces all sensitivity zeros to f(y)=(y-1)e^(19y)+20(20y-1). Certified alternating signs at 0,1/10,1/2,1 and the unique positive zero of f''(y)=(361y-323)e^(19y) prove exactly three simple roots. This gives precisely two depth-response maxima and one minimum. The one-band minimizer is explicit with exactly one derivative zero for every a,b>0. The proof shows z→0 at high attenuation. The standalone checker passed 32145 supplementary assertions, not used as the global proof.

value.rationale: The precise scientific gap is sensitivity of selected refuge depth to a changing attenuation environment when visual risk contains distinct exponential spectral components. Strict convexity gives uniqueness at each fixed attenuation, yet two independently attenuated risks yield two robustly isolatable crests in the optimizer response. A universal one-band one-crest theorem shows the effect cannot be captured by a simpler single-component approximation. This is a substantive mathematically motivated model-boundary counterexample, not a claim of empirical measurement or a routine parameter substitution.
